'''''Plocamium cartilagineum''''' is a medium-sized red marine alga.

==Description==
[[File:Plocamium cartilagineum Miller.jpg|thumb|Plocamium cartilagineum Miller]]
''Plocamium cartilagineum'' is an erect [[red alga]] growing to 10 cm in length. The main axes is flattened with regular flattened branches on both sides. The branches are long and short alternately, the short ones on one side are opposite the longer on the other side. These longer branches bear two or three short curved branches in series, comb-like. The plants are fully [[corticated]]. This branching pattern is similar to ''[[Plocamium lyngyanum]]'' and ''[[Plocamium maggsiae]]'' the other European species which have only recently been distinguished.<ref name="Bunker">Bunker, F.StP.D., Brodie, J.A., Maggs, C.A. and Bunker, A.R. 2017 ''Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland''. Second Edition. Wild Nature Press, Plymouth, UK {{ISBN|978-0-9955673-3-7}}</ref><ref>Dickinson, C.I. 1963. ''British Seaweeds''. The Kew Series</ref>

==Habitat==
Common on rock in the lower [[littoral]] and deeper to 30.<ref name="Bunker"/><ref name="Hardy">Hardy, F.G. and Guiry, M.D. 2003  ''A Check-list and Atlas of Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland.'' The British Phycological Society {{ISBN| 0-9527115-16}}</ref>

==Reproduction==
[[File:Plocamium cartilagineum cystocarps.jpg|thumb|left|Apical parts of a thalli of the red seaweed ''Plocamium cartilagineum'', with female reproductive structures ([[cystocarp]]s) visible.]]The plants are [[dioecious]]. The male structures are microscopic. The female [[cystocarp]]s grow to 1 mm in diameter and are on the margins of the frond. The [[spermatangia]] are within the youngest branches in [[Sorus|sori]]. The [[tetrasporangia]] are microscopic.<ref name="Bunker"/>

==Distribution==
Common all around the [[British Isles]] including [[Shetland]] and [[Channel Islands]].<ref name="Hardy"/>Faeroes and Norway to Senegal, Mediterranean and Canary Isles.<ref>Dixon, P.S. and Irvine, L.M. 1977. ''Seaweeds of the British Isles Volume 1 Rhodophyta Part 1 Introduction, Nemaliales, Gigartinales'' British Museum (Natural History) {{ISBN|0 565 00781 5}}</ref>
